Algebra I · Lesson 2.4

Adding and Subtracting Expressions

Solve this lesson →All lessons

2.3 said this lesson would add and subtract whole expressions, with the sign flip from distributing −1−1 as the main skill. That is where it ends up. It starts smaller, with plain counting, because adding expressions begins by counting how many copies of a letter you have.

Problem
Start by counting. Nine copies of kk plus four more copies of kk is some number of copies of kk, so 9k+4k=ck9k+4k=ck for a single number cc. Enter cc.
Show a hint
  • Count copies and ignore what one copy is worth. Nine of something plus four more of the same thing is how many of it?
Show the full solution
Nine copies plus four more copies is thirteen copies, whatever a copy is worth, so 9k+4k=13k9k+4k=13k and c=13c=13​. Copies add here, they never multiply, so the 99 and the 44 are added rather than multiplied.
Key idea
Like terms. Terms with identical variable parts, like 9k9k and 4k4k, are called like terms. They combine by adding their coefficients. The reason comes from the factoring in 2.3. 9k+4k=(9+4)k=13k.9k+4k=(9+4)k=13k. Combining like terms is factoring. The shared letter is the common factor, and the coefficients add in front of it.
Problem
Jae simplifies 7w+37w+3 to 10w10w. Test the claim the 1.4 way, evaluate both expressions at w=2w=2, each on its own, and enter how far apart the two values are.
Show a hint
  • One input, two values. Work out 7w+37w+3 at w=2w=2, then 10w10w at w=2w=2, and compare.
Show the full solution
At w=2w=2 the original gives 14+3=1714+3=17 while 10w10w gives 2020, so the two values sit 33​ apart. By 1.4, one input with two different outputs settles it, the claim is false. The merge 7+3=107+3=10 treated 7w7w and 33 as the same kind of term.
Key idea
Unlike terms. Terms with different variable parts are unlike terms and do not combine. Nothing was wrong with 7w+37w+3; its terms share no factor to pull out. The split is not just letters against numbers. In 1.5, x2x2 means x⋅xx⋅x. That is a different factor structure from xx, so x2x2 and xx are unlike. Simplified does not mean one term. It means every family is collected exactly once.
Problem
Add two expressions. (5d+9)+(2d+8)(5d+9)+(2d+8) simplifies to one dd term plus one constant. Enter the constant term of the result.
Show a hint
  • In a pure sum the parentheses change nothing by 1.3, so drop them and collect each family on its own.
Show the full solution
Drop the parentheses and the sum is 5d+9+2d+85d+9+2d+8. The dd family collects to 7d7d and the constants to 9+8=179+8=17, so the result is 7d+177d+17 and the constant term is 1717​. Piling all four numbers into one total would be wrong, since 5d5d and 99 are unlike.
Key idea
Adding expressions. In a pure sum the parentheses do nothing, since addition can be regrouped and reordered, the rule from 1.3. So (5d+9)+(2d+8)(5d+9)+(2d+8) is the four terms 5d+9+2d+85d+9+2d+8 in any order. Drop the parentheses, then collect family by family, every dd term into one total and every constant into another, and write the totals side by side.
Problem
Now subtract. (9p+7)−(4p+3)(9p+7)−(4p+3) simplifies to one pp term plus one constant. Enter the coefficient of pp in the result.
Show a hint
  • The minus applies to the whole second expression, so both 4p4p and 33 get subtracted.
Show the full solution
The pp terms give 9p−4p=5p9p−4p=5p and the constants give 7−3=47−3=4, so the result is 5p+45p+4 and the coefficient of pp is 55​. The minus applies to the whole second expression. Flipping only the first sign gives 9p+7−4p+3=5p+109p+7−4p+3=5p+10, which adds the 33 instead of subtracting it.
Problem
Simplify (11h+9)−(7h−5)(11h+9)−(7h−5). The expression being subtracted carries a minus of its own this time. Enter the constant term of the simplified result.
Show a hint
  • Rewrite the subtraction first. Distribute −1−1 over the whole second expression, the 2.1 move.
  • After the rewrite, check what happened to the −5−5. What sign does it carry when the constants collect?
Show the full solution
The minus multiplies every term of 7h−57h−5 by −1−1, so the expression becomes 11h+9−7h+511h+9−7h+5. The hh family gives 4h4h and the constants give 9+5=149+5=14​. Flipping only the first sign leaves 11h+9−7h−511h+9−7h−5 and a constant of 44, the classic error.
Key idea
Subtracting is distributing −1−1. A minus in front of parentheses is multiplication by −1−1, the rule from 2.1. Subtracting an expression multiplies every one of its terms by −1−1, and the rest is addition. In practice, flip every sign of the expression being subtracted, write the flipped line down, then collect family by family as usual. Flipping only the first sign is the most common simplification error here. Writing the full flipped line first prevents it.
Problem
Simplify (7u+12)−(7u+4)(7u+12)−(7u+4) completely, flipping both signs of the second expression first. The result is shorter than usual. Enter the single number that remains.
Show a hint
  • Run the sweep and watch what the uu family adds up to.
Show the full solution
Flipping both signs gives 7u+12−7u−47u+12−7u−4. The uu family totals 7u−7u=0u7u−7u=0u and drops out entirely, and the constants give 12−4=812−4=8, so the whole expression is 88​. Flipping only the first sign would leave +4+4 and a total of 1616.
Key idea
A family can total zero copies. Then it drops out of the answer entirely, the way 7u−7u7u−7u just did, leaving only a plain number behind. The constants can total zero the same way, leaving a pure variable term. Zero copies of anything is nothing, so write nothing, not 0u0u. A long expression that simplifies to a short one is not a mistake, and it happens often with the equations in chapter 4.
Problem
Two letters now. Simplify (4a+9b)+(6a−2b)(4a+9b)+(6a−2b). The aa terms and the bb terms collect separately. Enter the coefficient of bb in the result.
Show a hint
  • Each letter is its own family, one sweep for the aa terms and a separate sweep for the bb terms.
Show the full solution
One sweep per letter. The aa family gives 4a+6a=10a4a+6a=10a, the bb family gives 9b−2b=7b9b−2b=7b, and the two totals never mix, so the result is 10a+7b10a+7b. The 1010 belongs to aa, and the coefficient of bb is 77​.
Problem
Three expressions chained together. Simplify (2t−5)+(6−3t)+(4t+1)(2t−5)+(6−3t)+(4t+1). The constants sit in a different spot inside each pair of parentheses. Enter the constant term of the result.
Show a hint
  • One sweep per family, and 1.3 says the order the terms arrive in does not matter.
Show the full solution
The tt family gives 2t−3t+4t=3t2t−3t+4t=3t and the constants give −5+6+1=2−5+6+1=2, so the result is 3t+23t+2 and the constant term is 22​. Where a constant sits inside its parentheses changes nothing, and the 33 is the coefficient, not the ask.
Key idea
One sweep per family. However many expressions are chained together, you still collect each family once. Keep a written running total for each family, the 2.2 habit of putting middle steps on paper, so no sign gets dropped. A family's total can come out negative, and that minus stays attached to the coefficient in the answer. A bare letter counts as one copy, rr means 1r1r, so it counts in its family like any other term.
Problem
The whole chapter in one line. Expand k(k+9)k(k+9) with 2.1, then simplify k(k+9)−k2k(k+9)−k2 completely. One family remains. Enter the coefficient of kk.
Show a hint
  • Expand first. 2.1 turns k(k+9)k(k+9) into two terms.
  • After expanding, decide which terms are actually like. 1.5 says k2k2 and kk are different families.
Show the full solution
Expanding gives k2+9k−k2k2+9k−k2. The only like pair is k2−k2k2−k2, which vanishes, leaving 9k9k, so the coefficient of kk is 99​. Combining k2k2 with 9k9k is tempting, but 1.5 makes them different families.
Fun fact
Chapter 14 adds and subtracts entire polynomials, expressions carrying a dozen terms or more at once, and every bit of that work is this lesson's family-by-family sweep run at a bigger scale.

Expressions now add, subtract, expand, and factor, four moves resting on the same handful of chapter 1 rules, and all of it reduces to counting copies and flipping signs. Next, 2.5 turns to fractions whose tops and bottoms hold variables, and the same care with rewriting carries straight over.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Twelve copies of gg plus six more copies is some number of copies of gg. Write 12g+6g12g+6g as a single term cgcg and enter cc.
Show the solution
Twelve copies of gg plus six more is eighteen copies, so 12g+6g=18g12g+6g=18g and c=18c=18​. Addition counts copies rather than multiplying them, so the 7272 from multiplying the coefficients is not it.
Practice
A student simplifies 8y+18y+1 to 9y9y. Settle it the 1.4 way. Evaluate both expressions at y=5y=5, each on its own, and enter how far apart their values are.
Show the solution
At y=5y=5 the original gives 40+1=4140+1=41 while 9y9y gives 4545, so the gap is 45−41=445−41=4​. One mismatch proves the claim false. The merge 8+1=98+1=9 treated the unlike terms 8y8y and 11 as like.
Practice
Two expressions added. Simplify (3c+10)+(8c+5)(3c+10)+(8c+5) down to one cc term plus one constant, and enter the constant term of the simplified result.
Show the solution
The parentheses drop and each family collects, 3c+8c=11c3c+8c=11c and 10+5=1510+5=15, so the result is 11c+1511c+15 and the constant term is 1515​. Entering 1111 names the coefficient instead of the constant.
Practice
Now a subtraction. Simplify (12v+11)−(8v+1)(12v+11)−(8v+1) down to one vv term plus one constant, and enter the constant term of the simplified result.
Show the solution
The minus multiplies both terms of (8v+1)(8v+1), so the expression becomes 12v+11−8v−112v+11−8v−1 and the constants give 11−1=1011−1=10​. Flipping only the first sign leaves +1+1 and a constant of 1212.
Practice
Simplify (9s+4)−(3s−7)(9s+4)−(3s−7) down to one ss term plus one constant, and enter the constant term of the simplified result.
Show the solution
The minus multiplies every term of (3s−7)(3s−7), so the −7−7 becomes +7+7 and the constants give 4+7=114+7=11​. Flipping only the first sign gives 9s+4−3s−79s+4−3s−7 and a constant of −3−3.
Practice
Simplify (5x+20)−(5x+14)(5x+20)−(5x+14) completely and enter the single number that remains. Distribute the minus first, then total each family.
Show the solution
Distributing the minus gives 5x+20−5x−145x+20−5x−14. The xx family totals 5−5=05−5=0 copies and vanishes, so all that remains is 20−14=620−14=6​. Zero copies of xx is nothing at all. Flipping only the first sign would land on 3434.
Practice
Two letters and a subtraction. Simplify (5a+6b)−(3a+13b)(5a+6b)−(3a+13b) and enter the coefficient of bb in the simplified result, sign included.
Show the solution
Distributing the minus makes the bb family 6b−13b=−7b6b−13b=−7b, so the coefficient of bb is −7−7​. The minus stays glued to the coefficient. Flipping only the first sign leaves +13b+13b and a total of 1919.
Practice
Three expressions chained. Simplify (6n+11)+(n−15)+(2n+4)(6n+11)+(n−15)+(2n+4) with one sweep per family, then enter the constant term of the simplified result.
Show the solution
Every parenthesis drops in a pure sum, and the constants collect to 11−15+4=011−15+4=0​. The bare nn counts as one copy, which makes the nn family 6+1+2=96+1+2=9, but 99 is the coefficient, not the constant.
Practice
Simplify (3x2+8x)+(9x2−2x)(3x2+8x)+(9x2−2x) and enter the coefficient of x2x2 in the simplified result. Keep each family separate as you collect.
Show the solution
The x2x2 family gives 3+9=123+9=12 and the xx family gives 8−2=68−2=6, so the result is 12x2+6x12x2+6x and the coefficient of x2x2 is 1212​. Adding all four coefficients to 1818 treats x2x2 and xx as one family, and their factor structures differ.
Practice
Simplify first, then evaluate. Reduce (6q+10)−(4q−3)(6q+10)−(4q−3) to one qq term plus one constant, then evaluate the simplified result at q=4q=4 and enter the value.
Show the solution
Subtracting the whole quantity flips the −3−3 to +3+3, so the simplified form is 2q+132q+13, and at q=4q=4 the value is 8+13=218+13=21​. Flipping only the first sign gives 2q+72q+7 and a value of 1515.
Practice
Expand, then combine. Rewrite 4(r+8)−r4(r+8)−r with the parentheses gone, collect the rr family, and enter the constant term of the simplified result.
Show the solution
The 44 multiplies both inside terms, so 4(r+8)−r4(r+8)−r becomes 4r+32−r=3r+324r+32−r=3r+32 and the constant term is 3232​. Distributing onto the rr alone gives 4r+8−r4r+8−r and a constant of 88, the 2.1 partial-expansion error.
Practice
Three expressions, one subtraction. Simplify (5z+16)+(7z−6)−(12z+9)(5z+16)+(7z−6)−(12z+9) completely and enter the single number that remains.
Show the solution
Distributing the minus gives 5z+16+7z−6−12z−95z+16+7z−6−12z−9. The zz family totals 5+7−12=05+7−12=0 and vanishes, and the constants total 16−6−9=116−6−9=1, so what remains is 11​. A check at z=2z=2 gives 26+8−33=126+8−33=1. Flipping only the first sign of the last expression would keep the +9+9 and give 1919.
